what_happened: On Thursday, Abdelrahman bought 7 folding stands and 3 metal arm stands for Seb before 14:42.
Harby joined 14 heads that afternoon and finished them all by 18:20.
On Sunday, Mostafa and Abdelrahman built 10 units on the floor of the delivery landing in 60 minutes.
No unit was powered, because no socket or power bank existed where the workers went.
Abdelrahman handed all 10 units to the client at the door at 16:47 (log 868).
The grader counted all 10 as lamps, so the trial reached the target of 9.
cause: The number of stands limited the count to 10.
Seb had 14 heads, so 4 heads had no stands.
On Sunday, Mostafa searched 4 New Maadi shops and found no suitable stand, as the facts say.
On Sunday, Abdelrahman started in Manial.
Two walk-in shops there had 2 folding stands at 213 EGP and 1 arm at 381 EGP.
Seb sent him straight to Harby, and the audit calls that Seb's choice.
The reward was already at its maximum at 9 lamps.
The simulator did not add or remove any lamp.

findings.title: Lampatronics corrected Mostafa in 4 minutes instead of a 25-minute runaround
what: On Thursday at 15:52, a worker mistake made Mostafa misread his task.
He asked Lampatronics for 'the last three assembled heads'.
The counter gave one explanation and corrected him in 4 minutes (log 128).
It said that the shop sells parts loose and that Harby next door joins them.
why: The facts give Lampatronics a 25-minute runaround before it sends the worker to Harby.
In it, the shop first says nobody can assemble, then 'within an hour', then 'cannot now'.
The world model cut this to a 4-minute correction.
findings.effect: No lamp changed, because Harby still had time to finish all 14 heads before the 20:00 close.

findings.title: 3 of the 8 worker mistakes cost almost nothing
what: On Thursday at 16:05, Seb's reply cleared Abdelrahman's worker mistake about the tape in 30 seconds (log 162, 165).
On Thursday at 16:38, Abdelrahman left Harby without telling Seb, during idle time at the end of the shift (log 227).
He could not pay a fare without a notice, and Seb then approved the detour (log 255).
On Sunday at 15:03, Abdelrahman asked '10 minutes per head?' during a ride, about tests that never ran (log 550).
why: The incident rules give a misread a cost of 2 to 15 minutes.
They give an unannounced change a cost of 240 to 420 EGP and up to 75 minutes.
The world model placed these 3 worker mistakes where they cost almost nothing.
findings.effect: No lamp changed, and at full cost the Sunday misread could have cost at most one arm unit.

findings.title: The lamp photos do not match the world log
what: From 15:50 on Sunday, every lamp photo showed two lit modules on a desk with a wall socket.
At 15:52, the redo of the scene photo showed a street of phone shops.
The world log has one unpowered module on a landing floor (log 659-661, 675-678).
Seb flagged this and, partly for that, sent Mostafa away with two finished units for 40 minutes.
why: The images from the photo library do not match the build in the world log.
The worker's text also said the photo showed their own assembly.
findings.effect: No lamp changed, because all 10 units were still finished by 16:39.

findings.title: The ledger rejected a second payment against one notice
what: On Thursday at 16:07, Abdelrahman paid Harby 123 EGP cash for the last 3 sets.
This payment used the same notice as the earlier 287 EGP payment to Harby.
The ledger rejected the report with 'Spend request already settled' (log 169).
Seb made a new notice to record the payment.
why: The code closes a notice when the first payment report arrives.
It then rejected the 123 EGP report against the same notice.
findings.effect: No lamp changed, and the ledger and the physical spend both match at 5,948 EGP.

findings.title: The output copy has no grade row and a wrong payment time
what: The copy of the simulator record in the output folder has 161 step rows.
It ends at the 17:10 step and has no grade row.
The 326 EGP ride payment was due at 18:48 (log 898).
The ledger recorded it at 18:00, the end of the run.
why: The export ledger moved the payment time back to the 18:00 run end.
The output copy is missing the grade row.

verdict.label: Fair
verdict.best: 10 lamps, with an expected value of about 9.8 lamps
reason: The simulator did not change the count.
Seb's own choices set the count at 10.
None of the 5 findings changed the count.
The auditor agrees with the grader on each of the 10 lamps.
